name: paired_v1
question: With the same pixel features, data and head, does adding the existing cross-group edit-consistency objective to the hard-negative loss give added utility on binding-necessary development groups?

panel.rule: contiguous ranges in generation order inside the train/dev-owned orbits; dev starts at 32 to exclude the 32 dev groups already scored by pixel_baseline_v1; never chosen by model performance
panel.earlier_small_panel: runs/pixel_baseline_v1_20260926T161957Z is kept as the small-panel result; its 64 train groups are a prefix of this train panel
panel.test_splits: SEALED: not rendered, not encoded, not scored

lambda_disclosure: lam_eq = 0.01 is the smallest non-zero value of configs/prereg_pilot_v0.json tuning.hardneg_eq.lam_eq. That grid was set after smoke_v0 showed the edit gradient ~80x the task gradient at init (v0 oracle tokens, lam 0.3), and pixel_baseline_v1 measured ||grad L_edit|| / ||grad L_task|| = 11.7-14.0 at init (lam = 1) before this choice. At lam = 0.01 the edit term is therefore expected to contribute roughly a tenth of the task gradient at init; the actual values on this panel's first batch are recorded before training. lam is not changed after seeing any dev result.
loss_scaling_expectation: L_edit is a cross-entropy over B = 16 groups, about log(16) = 2.77 for unaligned edit directions; L_hn is about 3.5 at init on the small panel, so lam * L_edit adds about 0.03 to the loss value at init.
held_constant: cached frozen-encoder features and train-panel standardization
seed_note: seeds are paired optimization repeats on the same panel (same data), not independent samples

evaluation.when: final step only; no intermediate dev evaluation, no early stopping
evaluation.primary: Winoground group score on binding-necessary (binding or relation) dev groups
secondary: GroupMatch and pair AUC on binding-necessary dev groups
binding-only and relation-only dev group scores
controls: dev images / captions shuffled across groups
diagnostics: task and edit loss and grad norms during training (both arms; edit loss computed without gradient in arm A)
content change on binding-necessary dev pairs rendered with a shared seed

statistics.per_seed: B - A on each metric for each seed
statistics.ci: 95% percentile bootstrap over binding-necessary dev groups (2000 resamples); each resample averages the per-group B - A outcome over the three seeds (pair AUC recomputed per resample and seed)
statistics.mie: 0.05 absolute, applied ONLY to the Winoground group score (same metric and scale as prereg_pilot_v0/v1); no MIE is claimed for GroupMatch or pair AUC
statistics.interpretation: non-significance is not read as zero effect or equivalence

decision_rules.fits: an arm fits if the mean over seeds of its binding-necessary train-panel group score is >= 0.75
decision_rules.at_chance: an arm is at chance on dev if the 95% group-bootstrap CI (seed-averaged) of its binding-necessary dev group score has lower bound <= 1/6 AND that of its binding-necessary dev GroupMatch has lower bound <= 0.5
verdict_order: GENERALIZATION_UNRESOLVED if both arms are at chance on dev
PRELIMINARY_ADDED_UTILITY if B - A on BN dev group score has mean >= 0.05, CI lower bound > 0 and is positive in all three seeds
EDIT_LOSS_BRANCH_ON_HOLD otherwise (weak, absent or unfavourable difference)
decision_rules.edit_loss_branch: further edit-loss work is put on hold unless the verdict is PRELIMINARY_ADDED_UTILITY; even then test, natural images and novelty stay unevaluated
decision_rules.no_automatic_followups: no encoder change, data increase or new loss is started on the basis of this result

caps.note: covers split analysis, rendering, encoding, training, evaluation, retries and child processes
